You use wish, plus the past form of the verb or the past participle of the verb to talk about imaginary situations in the past, present or future.

Wishes and sentences in the second and third conditional infer that what you want is probably not possible, or for some reason impossible and that you regret what happened in the past.

You use wish + Simple Past to talk about wishes in the present or future.

For example:
Sometimes I wish I were a millionaire.

You use wish + could to talk about wishes for the future.

Example:
I wish I could be as generous as you.

You use wish + had + past participle to talk about wishes about past situations.

For example:
I wish I hadn't been there!
I wish I didn't have to work extra hours to pay off my student loan!
I wish I could be as generous as you.
Gosh, I wish I were a millionaire.
I wish I hadn't been there!
I wish I could have witnessed that.
The Third Conditional - Talking Hypothetically About the Past

You use the third conditional to talk about unreal situations in the past.
These are things that did not happen in the past. You often use the third conditional to talk about regrets.

When you want to talk about situations in the past in a hypothetical context (not real or necessarily true), you can use the structures would have, should have and could have.

Could have (+ past participle) means that something was possible in the past. It also means that you had the ability to do something in the past, but that you didn't do it.
Example: I could have walked away and they wouldn't have noticed.

Should have (+ past participle) means something would have been a good idea. However, you did not do it. You can use it to give advice about the past to someone when you are speaking to them. You can also use it to express regret about what you did or did not do.
Example: I should have known!

Use would have ( + past participle) to talk about something that you wanted to do but did not do.
Example: If I hadn't suggested going to the police station your whole love life would have been entirely different.

images.text:
Sally: I've decided that because you're on a strict budget, I'm taking you guys out to dinner after we see a Celtics game. If we hadn't had such a rough week, I would have never thought of it!
Peter: Something good must have happened to you! Gosh, I wish I were a millionaire.
Sally: At least you know one, though, technically, I am not a millionaire!
Vanessa: I wish I could be as generous as you.
Peter: Don't be regretful Vanessa. You must have forgotten how many times you have cooked us great meals. You give us a lot of moral support.

Vanessa: I suppose that's true. Sally?
Sally: Yes, V.
Vanessa: If you hadn't met Officer O'Grady, would you have decided to take us out?
Sally: I wish you would stop looking for information, but you know the answer is “yes”, partly.
Peter: Oh god! I should have known! It was so obvious! I wish I hadn't been there! Actually it was like I wasn't there. V, If only you had seen those two flirt! I could have walked away and they wouldn't have noticed.

Vanessa: How intriguing! If I had been there I would have laughed. I wish I could have witnessed that. I should have come along.
Sally: If I hadn't been the victim of identity theft, I wouldn't have met Shawn.
Peter: If I hadn't suggested going to the police station your whole love life would have been entirely different. You can thank me.
Vanessa: Well, I wish I didn't have to work extra hours to pay off my student loan! You guys go ahead and enjoy the game. I'll work and when I get home I'll watch the game on TV.
